title: Blocking On Retries
eyebrow: Design question · design loop fixes (parent issue #457) · asked during Build by the #460 builder

short.lead: Your pick 2A said the decided-for-aj check blocks a reply until it links a page, up to three blocks in a row. The builder for #460 (Decided-for-aj check) found that the plugin cannot block a retried reply today, and stopped to ask rather than choose. Today the end-of-reply check can stop a reply only the first time I send it. When I send it again (a retry), the check only reports the problem and the reply goes through (hook.py:123). The three-in-a-row limit exists only as a constant that no code reads (design_loop.py:1984), and the check's own message wrongly says a missing page keeps blocking. The same question decides how #461 (Page check blocks again for choices and decisions) is built.

items: hook.py lines 194-199 run the blocking checks only the first time I send a reply. On a retry, they only report.

Building this page set the new Held state, so I stopped the builder for #465 (Rerun limit counts reading a script as running it). Its saved work resumes after your answer.

choices: How should the decided-for-aj check and the page check block?
Block on retries too, up to three in a row

Only these two checks may block a retry. After three blocks in a row the reply goes through with a note naming the missing page, so a fault in the page builder cannot keep a session blocked while nobody is watching. Every other check keeps today's once-only rule. The check's message is corrected to match.
Block once, like the other checks

The reply is blocked once. If my retry still settles a point without a page, the reply goes through with a report. Simpler, but a second try can get past it, which is how decisions slipped through before.
Block on every retry, with no limit
Strictest. If the check wrongly flagged harmless wording, or the page builder broke, the session would stay blocked until you step in.
A matches the three-block limit you chose for the page rule in #283 (the automatic-pages build plan), and it is the only option where a retry cannot simply walk past the check.

wrapup.summary: The decided-for-aj check and the page check need permission to block a retry, which no check has today. One pick decides both.
